propositions: Six files sit within 7 lines of the 800-LOC module-size cap with combined high churn and fan-in, creating a maintenance hazard and blocking ordinary work like ticket d23e
llm/config.py at 793 LOC with only 7 lines of headroom has insufficient space for a single new configuration knob (10-16 lines typical cost)

Relieving high-churn modules via domain extraction, data-driven tables, or absorbing-verb extraction can reduce churn absorption without merely relocating mass, as demonstrated in ADR 0056's treatment of runner.py
Seam tests asserting per-file headroom targets and registry membership provide the structural defence against regrowth after per-function length gates were rejected as too high blast radius
After extraction, config.py dropped to 631 LOC (49 lines under enforced 700 target) and d23e successfully landed its deprecation alias without structural prerequisite, meeting the epic's core intent

Two relieved files (config.py, workflow_ops.py) plus two new modules (gate_context.py, decide_ops.py) with four seam guards prevent future regressions, while attest.py, passes.py, and signing.py remain at or near cap as known-remaining work
